annotations.title: Read Scripture word for word from a stored text

description: PURPOSE: Read the Bible word for word from a stored text, never from memory: a passage by reference, a verse in its context, every verse containing given words, one verse side by side in several translations, the Hebrew or Greek words behind a verse, the passages readers link to it, a check of whether quoted words are real Scripture, or the list of stored translations. The default text is the King James Version the app ships; about sixty stored public domain or freely licensed Bibles, with the Hebrew and Greek, are read by translation or language. WHEN TO USE: whenever you will quote or examine Scripture and know the reference or the words, or need to check a quotation before repeating it. WHEN NOT: verses for a feeling or need, a topic, the words of Jesus on a theme, or the verse of the day: find_scripture_for. A parable, doctrine or the gospel explained: learn_the_faith. MODES (required parameters in brackets): passage [reference] one verse, a range inside one chapter, or a whole chapter. context [reference] the passage with the verses around it (around, default 2). search [query] verses containing all the words, or an exact phrase in double quotes, a page at a time (book, testament, whole_words, limit, cursor, parallel). compare [reference] one verse in up to six translations side by side (translations, include_original). original_words [reference] each Hebrew or Greek word with its Strong's number, lexicon entry, parsing and the KJV words it became (strong keeps one number, e.g. "G25"). cross_references [reference] linked passages from OpenBible.info with votes (limit, include_text). verify [quote] checks the words against every held translation (reference optional). translations [none] every stored translation with language, canon and license (language filters; include_license_text). PARAMETERS: translation and language apply to passage, context, search and cross_references; compare takes a list in translations. Ranges across chapters are not supported. OUTPUT: mode, answered_by (the implementation used) and that mode's fields: passage gives ref, text, verses [{verse, text}], translation, translation_name, source, read_more; context gives passage, before and after; search gives total_matches, results and next_cursor; compare gives rows per translation; original_words gives verses[].words with strong, lemma, definition and morph; cross_references gives references with votes; verify gives verdict (verbatim, close_but_differs with a word diff, or not_found), best_match with SHA-256 hashes; translations gives the list. Every Scripture answer carries evidence (translation, license, corpus version, SHA-256 per passage) and content_layers. BEHAVIOR: read only and deterministic; the texts are bundled, no network call. An unparseable reference, an unknown translation, or a book a translation does not hold returns an error with try_instead; a search with no match returns count 0 and result_state empty. Parameters a mode does not use are ignored and named in ignored_params. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

around.description: For context: verses to read on each side (default 2).

book.description: For search: one book to search, e.g. "Psalms", "1 Cor".

cursor.description: Opaque paging token: next_cursor from the previous answer of the same call. Omit for the first page.

include_license_text.description: For translations: true returns each license statement in full.

include_original.description: For compare: true (default) adds the Hebrew or Greek line.

include_text.description: For cross_references: true (default) reads each linked passage; false returns references and votes only.

language.description: The person's BCP-47 language, e.g. "es", "pt-BR", "sw". Picks the best stored public domain or freely licensed Bible for it; translation wins over it.

limit.description: For search (page size, default 10, max 20) and cross_references (default 6, max 12).

mode.description: Which kind of answer: passage, context, search, compare, original_words, cross_references, verify, translations. Each mode, and the parameters it needs, is explained in the description.

parallel.description: For search: a translation id read beside each verse found, e.g. "kjv".

query.description: For search: words that must all appear ("mercy truth"), or an exact phrase in double quotes. Case-insensitive.

quote.description: For verify: the exact words to check, as they would be quoted.

reference.description: Book, chapter and optional verse or range as a reader writes it: "John 3:16", "Psalm 23", "1 Cor 13:4-7". Required for passage, context, compare, original_words and cross_references; optional for verify (the reference the words are attributed to).

strong.description: For original_words: keep only the words with this Strong's number, e.g. "G25" or "H1254".

testament.description: For search: "old" or "new" to search one testament.

translation.description: A stored translation id from read_scripture mode translations, e.g. "bsb", "web", "dra", "rv1909", "cuv". Default: the King James Version, or the best stored Bible for language.

translations.description: For compare: up to six translation ids, e.g. ["kjv","bsb","dra","rv1909"].

whole_words.description: For search: true (default) matches whole words only; false matches inside words.

name: read_scripture

answered_by.description: The implementation that answered (the same tool name the signed-in endpoint lists).

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

ignored_params.description: Parameters given that this mode does not use.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: Read Scripture word for word from a stored text
